fair_value.method: Blend of a conservative intrinsic SOTP ($6.5), a peer/strategic-multiple SOTP ($11.4), a 2027 pro forma EV/sales check ($7.9) and a small weight on consensus analyst target ($24.15), all on ~331M pro forma shares (249.9M + ~15M ASM + 65.9M VAC) and ~$650M pro forma net debt after the $718M VAC cash payment (the $700M converts at $20.34 are treated as debt).

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Conservative intrinsic NAV. Uranium $850M (about 1.8-2.0M lb/yr at ~$85 realized vs ~$40/lb all-in cost, so ~$90M/yr EBITDA over a limited mine life, plus development pipeline); REE portfolio $800M risked (White Mesa Phase 1B/1C $300M, Donald 12.7%->49% earn-in $150M, Vara Mada/Bahia $150M, ASM Dubbo+Korean Metals Plant $200M vs $299M paid); VAC $1.4B (~$100M 2028E EBITDA x 14, vs $29M 2025 adj. EBITDA and $65-75M Sumter run-rate target); vanadium/HMS/isotopes $50M; capitalized corporate overhead -$300M. EV $2.8B less $650M net debt = $2.15B / 331M sh.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Peer/strategic-premium SOTP (what the market paid for Western critical-minerals exposure). Uranium $1.2B (~1.0x P/NAV at $96.50 LT price plus a premium as the largest US producer); REE $1.5B; VAC at deal EV $2.04B ($1.9B equity + $140M net debt); overhead -$300M. EV $4.44B less $650M net debt = $3.79B / 331M sh.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: 2027E pro forma revenue ~$650M (uranium ~1.8M lb x $85 = ~$150M, REE ~$20M, VAC ~$480M assuming an early-2027 close) x 5.0x (a premium to the ~5.3x non-ferrous industry forward P/S for magnet/US-supply scarcity) = $3.25B EV, less $650M net debt = $2.6B / 331M sh.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Consensus 12-month analyst target (8 analysts, Strong Buy; range includes BMO $18, Roth $16, HCW $29.25). Given low weight because most targets predate the sector de-rating and are anchored to the $16-28 trading range.

bear.story: US-China easing keeps deflating the rare-earth scarcity premium, VAC closes at a now-rich ~70x trailing EBITDA with integration and ramp costs, and REE Phase 1B/1C slips. Uranium drifts back to $70s, 2027 stays loss-making (consensus EPS only $0.03), and the stock trades toward conservative NAV around 5-7.

base.story: VAC closes in early 2027 and ASM integrates. Uranium holds $85-95 spot with LT near $96 and US production of ~2M lb at $23-30/lb cost. Heavy REE circuit construction stays on track for late 2027, and Donald reaches FID. The market values the company near a peer-multiple SOTP, but ~331M shares and $700M of converts cap the upside.

bull.story: Trade tensions re-flare or new Chinese export controls, plus US government support (OSC $725M loan finalized, possible price floors or offtakes like the MP/DoD deal), re-rate Western mine-to-magnet platforms. Sumter shows a credible path to 4,000 tpa ($130-140M EBITDA), uranium LT exceeds $100, and the stock recovers toward the $18-24 analyst range.

thesis_break_reason: Around $7 the equity is worth only the conservative intrinsic SOTP (~$6.5) with nothing paid for REE optionality. Trading there would most likely mean something fundamental went wrong: the VAC deal failed or needed dilutive rescue financing, the OSC loan fell through, heavy-REE construction or feed (Donald FID) stalled, or uranium prices collapsed. That is more than beta to the rare-earth sentiment trade.

catalysts.event: Q3-2026 results; 2027 uranium restart/production plan (up to +600k lb/yr expansion)

VAC acquisition close (regulatory/FDI approvals; issue 65.9M shares, $718M cash; Ara 19.9% holder)
OSC $725M conditional loan finalization after due diligence
FY2026 results and 2027 guidance, first consolidated outlook incl. ASM
US-China rare earth trade/export-control developments; US critical-minerals policy
Q2-2027 results; White Mesa Tb/Dy circuit construction progress (target end-2027)

key_uncertainties: Whether the rare-earth scarcity premium keeps deflating as US-China tensions ease, or reverses
VAC execution: paying ~$2.04B EV for ~$29M 2025 EBITDA only works if Sumter ramps to $65-75M and then 4,000 tpa
Dilution and leverage: ~331M pro forma shares, $700M converts plus a $250M term loan, and possible further equity to fund Phase 2, Vara Mada and the American Metals Plant
Uranium price path (spot ~$90, LT $96.50) and 2027 sales volumes/contract book
Timing of the heavy REE circuits (late 2027), Donald FID and Madagascar fiscal terms for Vara Mada
ASM share issuance count not confirmed in the sources I found (assumed ~15M)
reasoning: UUUU (Energy Fuels) closed at $11.35, near its 52-week low and down 59% from the $27.90 high. The fall came from a sector-wide de-rating of US rare-earth and uranium names as US-China trade tensions eased, from widening losses (Q2-26 net loss $0.13/sh; consensus 2026 EPS -$0.25, 2027 +$0.03; Zacks estimates revised down), and from dilution worries after the $1.9B VAC deal (65.9M shares plus $718M cash) and the all-stock ASM acquisition. The operations are sound: US uranium output at ~$23/lb cost, 2026 guidance reached by mid-year, spot ~$90 and LT at a record $96.50, $996M of working capital at 6/30, and heavy REE circuits under construction with Tb/Dy qualified by a large Japanese magnet maker. But the equity is now a leveraged, stock-funded roll-up. Pro forma it has ~331M shares and ~$650M net debt, and VAC is being bought at ~70x trailing EBITDA. My conservative SOTP gives ~$6.5, a peer-multiple SOTP ~$11.4 and EV/sales ~$7.9. With a 10% weight on the $24 consensus, the blended fair value is ~$10.4, slightly below spot. Sell-side targets ($16-29) look stale relative to the de-rating. Given 89% realized vol, a mid-cap commodity/thematic name and binary policy catalysts, I used a lognormal with a median of ~$11 (a small discount to spot, reflecting fair value below price and negative momentum, offset by analyst support and policy optionality) and sigma ~0.70, which is below trailing realized vol because some of that vol came from the 2025 mania. That gives a ~48% chance of finishing above today's price, ~25% below $6.81 and ~20% above $19.86. The bear/base/bull (6 / 11.5 / 21 at 25/50/25%) fits this ladder. I did not use option-market data.
